I went to Insadong Jar Sujebi!

- I visited around 12 o'clock on a weekday, but there was a bit of a wait, and since it was lunch time, many nearby office workers came.
- The price seems to be more popular these days because it is cost-effective compared to the current price.
- The food came out about 10 minutes after ordering, and there was kimchi on each table so you could eat as much as you wanted. Kimchi is delicious
- The sujebi is not thick, so it goes down easily. If the dough is thick, it tastes like flour, but I liked that it didn't have much of that taste, and it was very chewy. It feels like a handmade swallow rather than a machine handmade one.
- Perilla seed sujebi is so savory that you can't stop eating it, while spicy sujebi is spicy and refreshes your stomach. Although it is spicy, it is not spicy. I really enjoyed both of them.
- Except for perilla sujebi, oysters are included in sujebi. You can opt out if you tell us in advance. I usually don't eat oysters, but when I ate them cooked, it was okay without any discomfort.
- The jar interior creates a quiet atmosphere inside the store. It's a very popular restaurant, so it's a bit crowded, but the food and atmosphere are so good that I want to visit again.

reviews.text:
I went in with my boyfriend while thinking about what to eat for dinner, and it was a decision I have no regrets about.
✅ Menu Review: Garlic Bossam & Chive Pancake
• Garlic bossam: I was surprised that the bossam meat was really soft and had no unpleasant smell. In particular, the generous amount of garlic sauce on top was the best. It had a sweet yet spicy flavor without the garlic's unique spiciness, so it went well with the meat. If you eat it with kimchi, it melts in your mouth!
• Chive pancake: I ordered chive pancake because I felt bad about eating only bossam, but I wonder what I would have done if I hadn't ordered it. It is the epitome of ‘chewy on the outside’, crispy on the outside and moist on the inside. It was fragrant and savory with plenty of chives, so it had a taste that reminded me of makgeolli.
✅ Atmosphere and service
The interior of the store has a Hanok feel, so it has the unique feel of Insa-dong. The lighting was soft, so the atmosphere was great for a dinner date while chatting with my boyfriend. The staff were friendly and I was able to have a pleasant meal.
✅ Overall review
If you want to try authentic Korean food in Insa-dong or are looking for a restaurant that won't fail on a date, I definitely recommend it. Be sure to try the combination of the addictive taste of garlic bossam and crispy chive pancakes! 200% intention to visit again.

reviews.text:
A place where you can feel the comfort of a traditional pub and the taste of Korea

This restaurant may be a good choice for those looking for a different experience. The perilla oil makguksu, Jalpajin Hansang, and Song Myeong-seop's raw makgeolli that I ordered all showed Korea's special taste and aroma in themselves. The seasoning was not strong, so the overall taste of the food was bland, but it allowed me to better enjoy the natural taste of each ingredient.

The store itself is a little small, but the cozy interior, with an atmosphere befitting a traditional pub, made me feel comfortable. In that sense, the time spent here enjoying a sip of makgeolli on a rainy day will feel even more valuable.

If you come here as a couple, a couple, or a couple, it will be a place where you can make precious memories. I highly recommend this restaurant to those looking for the taste and atmosphere of a traditional pub.

reviews.author: Andrew Kim
reviews.text: Previously, I was planning to visit 'Dining in Space', a French fine dining restaurant run by chef Noh Jin-seong, because of its 1 Michelin star and unique view of Changdeokgung Palace, but I postponed it and it closed in March 2020, so I settled in there and went to 'Myomi', a Korean fine dining restaurant currently run by chef Jeong-mook Kim, for dinner. The reputation of having a view of Changdeokgung Palace and having 1 Michelin star still remains. It wasn't a window seat, but it had a good view of the window and the table was spacious compared to the window seat. (The window seat is a round table.) It was a single menu, so I only had to choose a drink or alcohol to go with it, and I ordered non-alcoholic sparkling wine to fit the group of people who don't drink alcohol. The appetizer that marks the start of the summer menu is served on a round plate with a small green tree reminiscent of a forest standing at the center, and the mist is trapped by the lid of a transparent, elongated glass container. As I lift the glass lid from my seat and gently turn it in front of my eyes, I smell something refreshing. After raising expectations with a great performance, horned conch, octopus, and beef jerky are served as an amuse bouche. Hornsora is made with fish cakes and served wrapped in fried tapioca. The texture is really good. Octopus chohoe is served on top of crispy snacks, topped with flower petals and coriander. As expected, the unique texture was impressive. Beef jerky is served on squid ink bread with beef jerky and truffles. Unlike the commonly eaten beef jerky, it has a softer texture. The next menu is Squid Farm, a combination of potato pancakes and squid. The texture of the potato pancakes is very crispy. Next is tomato & tuna, where you pour the broth over the tomatoes with tuna in it. The next menu is seasoned snow crab, which is snow crab bibimbap covered in fluffy foam and topped with shrimp paste. The seasoning wasn't too strong and it was light, so I enjoyed it quite a bit. Next is the seasonal fish & bean soup. It is a menu where white fish (I think it was croaker) is topped with an unusually green bean soup. I found that the taste of the bean soup goes surprisingly well with the fish. Next is the duck, which the chef brings out beforehand to show you the level of cooking, and then serves it with beets decorated like flowers. It was so soft and delicious. Next, before the main course of Korean beef, refreshing bae sikhye is served as a glenzer. It is very different from ground pears. Although the sweetness is quite restrained, you can clearly feel that it is sikhye. Next was the Korean beef steak. The taste of the meat was as good as I expected, and what was unique was that it came with ssamjang sauce, which went really well with it. Dessert includes ice cream with watermelon & rhubarb, mango, and corn, and three finger foods to enjoy with tea or coffee. It was a happy meal with a great view, atmosphere, and menu items that showed the chef's thought and sincerity in each item. It's a great place for couples or lovers to celebrate an anniversary or date.

reviews.author: ch. “Connoisseur” Paik
reviews.text:
Cheonha Bossam (3.9/5.0)
- When you want to eat soft front leg bossam and sweet kimchi

One-line review: A Bossam restaurant that ruled the world under the Bukchon sky with its generous portion and softness

As you slowly head north along Gyedong-gil, you will become immersed in the scale of Korea's traditional city and feel at ease. This is a small restaurant located at the eastern end of the quiet Bukchon area, overlooking the walls of Changdeokgung Palace. It is popular as a lunch restaurant for nearby office workers, a resting place for visitors to Bukchon to recharge their energy, and is also a famous restaurant where foreign tourists come to experience the taste and atmosphere of Korea. There is always a wait during peak lunch hours, but the turnover rate is not bad, so it's worth the wait.

The new black and white sign that is currently hanging appears to be the result of an administratively promoted ‘sign improvement project.’ It looks neat, but I miss the old, clunky signboard with the big serif letters. When I entered the restaurant after waiting, it was noisy. The atmosphere of a restaurant perfect for makgeolli is filled with diners. Many long-established restaurants in the old city center are moving away from the 'sit-down floors' and installing 'standing tables', but this restaurant still insists on the 'sit-down style' and requires you to take off your shoes, which is somewhat unfamiliar. I sit down and order the signature menu, ‘Bossam Jeongsik’. As I perused the menu posted on the wall, I was able to choose from two menus, 'Bossam Set Meal' and 'Bossam (Special) Set Meal', but before I knew it, only the 'Bossam Set Meal' menu remained, and the price had reached 16,000 won, which was an increase from the previous price of 'Bossam (Special) Set Meal'.

While the meat is being cut in the kitchen, four side dishes and bossam kimchi are placed, along with ssam vegetables, garlic, and ssamjang. Japchae and steamed egg are frequent side dishes, and side dishes such as seasoned vegetables change depending on the season. All the side dishes are well seasoned and it feels faithful to the basics. It's not quite a table setting for a country dinner, but it's a table full of simple affection. Today’s wrap vegetable is perilla leaves, not lettuce. Due to the soaring price of food, 'cabbage kimchi', which is as important as the meat in 'Bossam set meal', has been changed to 'radish seasoning filling'. Now that the 'main character' has been replaced, I hope that the other actors will repay me with quality, but that doesn't seem to be the case.

Bossam meat has arrived. It looks great stacked in layers on a small plate, but it doesn't feel like a lot of food. This restaurant specially makes bossam meat by boiling 'jeonji', the front leg of a pig. Moist lean meat without any unpleasant odor forms the 'main' part, and soft fat serves as the 'sub', and the ratio of lean meat is higher than that of regular pork belly or pork neck bossam. However, it has a soft texture and a decent taste, which makes you wonder about the exquisite way it was boiled. If you prefer soft bossam, it may not be the texture you want. It is cut diagonally, so each piece is of a different size, and because it is generally cut in large chunks, it is quite satisfying to take a bite. The goal of this bossam is to make each and every piece honest and heavy without falling apart.

The 'radish seasoned filling', which was supposed to be 'cabbage kimchi', has a clean taste with a harmonious combination of spicy and sweet, and it seems clear that it was created for Bossam. Spread the perilla leaves and spread the salted shrimp meat on top. Fill the empty space with neatly seasoned radish kimchi and go straight into your mouth. The tenderness of the meat and the cleanliness of the seasoning intersect. If you add soybean paste stew every now and then, the meat plate will run out before you know it. Although it satisfied my hunger, I feel that it is not enough to satisfy my gastronomic cravings. There is no need to compare price/performance with a delicious meal, but with a disappointing meal, you have to think carefully about the skyrocketing price.

Although the cost of the table is soaring, the exorbitant prices and the unfinished table leave something to be desired, 'Cheonha Bossam' still claims to be the best bossam in the world.

reviews.author: A house that only tastes good
reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in steamed monkfish
Located a 3-minute walk from Jongno 3-ga Station.
A small size seafood stew costs 50,000 won.

Between monkfish and seafood~
I thought about it for a moment because the name is monkfish stew, but
I tried steamed seafood, which I had always wanted to eat.
The price wasn't as cheap as I thought, but it included 2 abalone and 2 octopuses.
In addition, squid, roe, shrimp, crab, mussels, and vegetables.
The octopus was better than I expected, but I was disappointed that the crab I was looking forward to had a slight smell.
I guess monkfish was better than seafood after all.
The sauce lacked flavor and was a bit boring.
I was able to season it with soy sauce, but I was a little disappointed because I was expecting the taste of the seasoning.
Still, my friend who went with me said it was okay.
This kind of stew is meant to be enjoyed for the crunchy texture of the bean sprouts and the rich flavor of the sauce, but it was disappointing because it wasn't enough.
The dongchimi soup that came as a side dish was delicious.

Store & Tips & Review
Although the store is small, it is said that there is seating on the second floor of the building.
There are two menus: seafood and monkfish.
Price-wise, the large size seems to have more merit.
Order at the table and pay at the counter when you leave.
There are many places selling monkfish and seafood stew around here, and I went into this place after seeing the sign for Baeknyeon Store.
I think most of the taste will be similar.
When I was young, I think I ate steamed seafood for 20,000 to 30,000 won, but now it's too expensive to pay for it.
I think this menu would be good for a company dinner.
Young people prefer seafood stew, while middle-aged people prefer monkfish stew.
